- Keep right to assume defense for third-party infringement claims and reserve reimbursement-only for output/regulatory liabilities.

Sean — thanks for the summary. I read Kestrel's redline and sketched some language and a narrow process below. My preference is to avoid conceding control of defense for third-party IP claims. Practical compromise we can offer: a two-track flow that differentiates (A) third-party asserted IP claims and (B) customer-litigated/regulatory claims tied to model outputs.

Suggested clause (high level):
- For asserted third-party IP claims alleging infringement by the Platform, Redwood shall have the right to assume and control the defense, provided Redwood promptly notifies Customer and (if requested in writing) retains counsel reasonably satisfactory to Customer. If Redwood elects not to assume defense, Redwood will reimburse Customer for reasonable, documented defense costs up to the capped amount set in the Order Form, subject to Customer providing the evidence checklist and cooperating with Redwood.
- For claims arising from Customer prompt/content or regulatory obligations (i.e., output liability), parties will follow an expedited evidence-and-remediation path: Customer must submit the evidence checklist within 10 business days of notice; Redwood will evaluate within 5 business days and propose remediation. Reimbursement is limited to documented remediation costs and excludes consequential losses.

Practical points / reasons:
- Right-to-defend is standard and lets us control litigation strategy and settlement.
- Reimbursement-only path for output/regulatory scope meets their ask without broadening our indemnity.
- Require evidence checklist (see attached) and short SLA windows to prevent stale claims and to keep forensic work feasible.

I can produce a tracked redline tonight if you want to use it on tomorrow's call. Also note we should loop in Procurement for any escrow threshold concessions and run the insurance ask by Finance.

—Kimberly

Hi Ben / Sean — thanks for sending your proposed approach. A few clarifications from Kestrel's side and our constraints:

1) Defense control: We operate under strict regulatory oversight for certain therapeutics workstreams and, for allegations that relate to clinical decisioning or outputs that touch PHI-like workflows, our counsel has to control defense decisions for compliance reasons. We are not asking Redwood to be exposed to open-ended remediation without the ability to control the technical response.

2) Escrow/threshold: Our procurement asks for a low escrow trigger ($250k) with automatic release to the customer upon verified remediation completion. We understand Redwood's desire to control litigation — our ask is a clear path to remediation funds when evidence is demonstrable.

3) Evidence: attaching our redline and a sample evidence bundle for claims related to model output. We can commit to a 7-business-day window to produce evidence if Redwood commits to a short review SLA.

We'd prefer to talk through this on a quick call. Proposed times: Thu 11am PT or Fri 9am PT.
